issue: MAC retry vs application ARQ interaction: backoff consistency with 10% jitter
evidence_quote: CEEPEW_ARQ_MAX_RETRIES=3U, CEEPEW_ARQ_TIMEOUT_MS=600U, CEEPEW_ARQ_HOP_SPAN_EXTRA_ATTEMPTS=1U, CEEPEW_ARQ_EFFECTIVE_ATTEMPTS=5. Exponential backoff shift: 100, 200, 400ms clamped; 4th attempt reuses 400ms. Worst-case per-fragment delivery: (1+3+1)×600+(100+200+400+400)=4100ms. Registry ARQ-WORST confirms: "5 * 600 ms + 100 + 200 + 400 + 400 = 4100 ms".
location: components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h lines 103-121; paper §III.D; results/registry.json ARQ-WORST entry
minimal_fix: None required; backoff model is internally consistent. The '245-753ms' observed range is not directly explained by the worst-case 4.1s model — likely represents successful-retries-before-exhaustion subset, or measurement scope differs from theoretical worst case.

issue: Airtime model: 1Mbps assumption, long preamble, 39B overhead, MAC ACK duration
evidence_quote: Registry AIR-249-MPDU: formula '192 us + (249 + 39) * 8 us' = 2.528 ms. AIR-ACK: '192 us + 14 * 8 us' = 0.304 ms. AIR-DATA-ACK: '2.528 ms + 0.010 ms + 0.304 ms' = 2.84 ms. Paper intro: '288B of frame, 4B of FCS, and 192μs of PLCP.' 1Mbps = 8μs/byte. 192us/8us = 24B PLCP. 2.528ms = 2528μs = 316B total = 288B frame + 4B FCS + 24B PLCP. ACK = 14B @ 1Mbps long preamble, 0.304ms = 304μs = 24B + 14×8μs.
location: results/registry.json AIR-249-MPDU, AIR-ACK, AIR-DATA-ACK entries; paper §IV.B; paper Introduction
minimal_fix: The 39B overhead in AIR-249-MPDU formula yields 2.496ms computed vs 2.528ms stated — a 32μs/4B discrepancy. Either the formula implicitly includes 4B FCS not counted in 39, or the stated value rounds differently. MAC ACK duration (0.304ms) correctly matches 14B + PLCP at 1Mbps long preamble.

issue: 18ms send-callback vs ~2.5ms airtime: sources of 15ms gap
evidence_quote: LAT-LITE-CB: send-callback latency median 18.0ms (N=76). Paper §650-651 and line 666: 'the send-callback median of 18.0ms (N=76) sits ≈15ms above the computed airtime, and FreeRTOS/UART overhead is the hypothesized cause.' Registry LAT-SUM-NONADDITIVE: 'med(CPU)=10.0 ms + med(CB)=18.0 ms = 28.0 ms, vs med(total)=27.0 ms (N=76); residual 1.0 ms within the cycle-model-to-latency gap.' Components of 18ms CB: 10.0ms cycle-converted CPU time + remaining ~8ms driver/stack overhead. Gap of ~15ms between 18ms CB and ~2.5ms airtime attributable to FreeRTOS scheduling, ESP-NOW driver processing, GPIO14 pulse gen/detect, and UART telemetry overhead.
location: results/registry.json LAT-LITE-CB, LAT-SUM-NONADDITIVE entries; paper Table 654-662; paper §666
minimal_fix: No fix needed; gap is documented and attributed to documented overhead sources (FreeRTOS/UART). The 10ms CPU conversion + 18ms CB = 28ms vs observed 27ms total is consistent within 1ms residual.

issue: Channel hopping: 9-channel, 5s epoch, HMAC-SHA256 keyed; in-frame loss at hop boundaries; histogram measured vs schedule-derived
evidence_quote: Transport hop design: 9 channels (CEEPEW_HOP_CHANNELS=9), 5s epoch (CEEPEW_HOP_INTERVAL_MS=5000ms), HMAC-SHA256 PRF keyed with ascon_key[0:16] and session_id for Fisher-Yates perm of {1..9}. Paper §386: 'Frequency diversity uses 9 channels, shifting every 5 seconds.' Paper §501: 'Hopping therefore remains a design property claim; no per-channel occupancy distribution is offered.' Paper §386: 'A replica of the shipped derivation over the first 2,000 epochs, about 2.8h of session time, produces 24 changes spaced 64 epochs (320s) apart.' 'The intended dwell is one epoch; the dwell in the build evaluated here is 320s. We report that as a defect in the build, not as a property of the design.' Outside capture runs (line 427): 'radios hold channel 1, keeping every frame visible to a fixed-channel observer.'
location: components/transport/transport_hop.c; paper §386 'Reliability Engineering...'; paper §501; paper line 427
minimal_fix: Build defect: evaluated runs have 320s dwell instead of intended 5s epoch. No code change required to fix the design — the 320s dwell is a build configuration issue. In-flight frame loss at hop boundaries is unlikely given 5s epoch >> 2-3ms frame transmission time, assuming lock-step hop derivation between peers.

issue: FEC justification: Hamming(15,11) with 802.11 FCS filtering; zero corrections observed; overhead justified?
evidence_quote: Paper §377-383 'Session-Permuted Hamming(15,11) FEC vs. IEEE 802.11 FCS': 'Hamming(15,11) adds 33-62B per frame and the 802.11 receiver already drops frames that fail its own FCS before they reach the ESP-NOW callback; consequently, on a clean LOS link the FEC layer can only add overhead without correcting errors that matter.' 'Across the 11 archived capture runs, therefore, zero software FEC bit corrections were triggered.' 'FEC-ON carried 50 messages by 499.5s. FEC-OFF completed 45 within 600s. Delivery was indistinguishable between arms: 50/53 (94.3%) against 45/48 (93.8%).' 'Each arm corrected 0 single-bit errors, and the ~1ms LOS channel offered nothing correctable, so the result confirms the design prediction: the parity cost buys nothing on this link.' Registry MEM-REGION-POOL and frame budget Table II confirm 33-62B overhead.
location: paper §377-383; results/registry.json entries for FEC overhead; components/transport/transport_esl.c stage_esl_crc stage 4
minimal_fix: FEC is not justified for this LOS link. The 33-62B per-frame parity cost provides zero error correction benefit since 802.11 FCS already drops corrupted frames. The ablation-confirmed null result (delivery identical with FEC ON/OFF) supports removing FEC from the default shipping build. An ablation arm preserving FEC-enabled build should remain available for research.

location: results/registry.json provenance footnote; paper Table 614; components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h CEEPEW_FEC_DISABLE lines 261-265
minimal_fix: Lite measurements are not affected by Full's -Og/-O2 flags — they use unoptimized builds from separate campaigns. However, the different optimization levels mean Full and Lite metrics are not directly comparable. FEC toggle (CEEPEW_FEC_DISABLE) is a compile-time switch that changes wire size and efficiency numbers for both profiles.

issue: Zero-heap claim precision: what 'no application-level heap' guarantees given mbedTLS/BLE/Wi-Fi internal allocations
evidence_quote: Paper §171: 'guarantees no application-level heap allocation (Δheap,app = 0B; the PSA, BLE, and Wi-Fi stacks still allocate internally).' Registry MEM-REGION-POOL: 'Static region allocator pool size for zero application-level heap allocation: 48KB.' Registry MEM-STACK-CORE0: 'Core 0 FreeRTOS UI task stack allocation: 10240B.' Registry MEM-STACK-CORE1: 'Core 1 FreeRTOS Session & Crypto task stack allocation: 16384B.' Table 659: 'Static region pool HWM (49,152B) & app heap delta Static: 1,376-5,152B (2.8-10.5%), Δheap,app=0B.' Threat model Table 563: 'Physical SRAM extraction & Disclosed: Keys zeroed on teardown, but reside in SRAM without eFuse/secure enclave binding.' Paper §728: 'The allocation claim is likewise scoped: no application-layer call reaches a heap allocator, while mbedTLS PSA and the Wi-Fi driver allocate internally and sit outside the claim.'
location: paper §171; results/registry.json MEM-REGION-POOL, MEM-STACK-CORE0, MEM-STACK-CORE1, TABLE 659 entries; threat model Table 563; paper §728
minimal_fix: The 'no application-level heap' guarantee (Δheap,app = 0B) is precise and correct for the CEE-PEW application code only. mbedTLS PSA, BLE, and Wi-Fi stacks allocate internally outside the claim. The 48KB region pool lives in .bss segment, not flash-encrypted. Keys are zeroed with ceepew_secure_zero() at teardown but reside in unprotected SRAM. No code change needed — the claim scope is correctly bounded.
